title: HNeRV frame embedding Mirror coordinate frontier
amendment: 01 single-video official checkpoint frame-embedding mechanism screen
scope: One Bunny video only. Measures actual quantized latent-code storage, held-out reconstruction PSNR and CPU decode cost; not multi-video generalization or NerVast comparison.

video.resolution: 1280x720 source; center crop 640x1280 to match model output

hypothesis: A shared latent basis plus small per-frame Mirror coordinate m can reduce HNeRV content-adaptive embedding bytes while preserving held-out frame PSNR and decode FPS; compare against ordinary PCA/low-rank coordinates to test Mirror specificity.
physical_object: Pinned HNeRV image decoder and one shared basis over the official 128-D per-frame embedding.
mirror_coordinate: m_t = Q_r^T(z_t - mean), synthesized by mean + Q_r m_t.
logical_multiplicity: 132 frame-specific decoder inputs represented by one common basis and per-frame coordinates.
controls: ordinary PCA/low-rank basis plus coordinates (same functional parameterization)

development.selection_metric: No hyperparameter chosen from audit; report frozen rank sweep.

fresh.reason: One fixed official checkpoint/video; frame-index split is the unit of held-out evaluation.

metrics: Mirror-vs-PCA output and byte alias check
success_gate: At least one rank reduces full deployment bytes by ≥10%, retains native mean audit PSNR within 0.25 dB, and achieves ≥90% native CPU FPS.
failure_gate: All ranks miss quality or latency gate, or the Mirror code exactly aliases the ordinary PCA/low-rank control; report all frontier points regardless.
boundaries: Single Bunny checkpoint only; no independent scene/video capacity claim.
This rank-code mechanism may be ordinary low-rank compression; Mirror-specific value requires a non-aliasing gain over PCA.
No NerVast result, bitrate/entropy coding, GPU decode, or general HNeRV training claim.
